concepts.title: Entrepreneur Roles and Qualities
concepts.definition: From the French enterprendre, to undertake, the entrepreneur plays three parts at once - innovator bringing new products, organiser assembling the factors of production, and risk bearer shouldering every uncertainty - and does so with initiative, industry knowledge, calculated risk-taking, adaptability, self-confidence and a wealth-creating drive that turns ideas into employment and capital.
concepts.key_idea: Innovate, organise, and carry the risk - backed by initiative, adaptability and self-belief, these are the entrepreneur's job description.
question_patterns: define the term entrepreneur from its French root and state the three prominent roles an entrepreneur fulfils
list any four qualities of a successful entrepreneur with brief explanations
differentiate an entrepreneur from an intrapreneur on the basis of employment and risk
how do entrepreneurs help in capital creation and employment generation
which qualities let an entrepreneur withstand the short-term risks of a new venture
why is entrepreneurship called a panacea for unemployment in an economy

solution_steps.explain: Innovator, organiser and risk bearer cover the entrepreneur's functions.
Initiative, knowledge, risk-taking, adaptability, self-confidence and wealth creation mark the successful ones.
An intrapreneur innovates inside an organisation without bearing the entrepreneur's personal risk.

worked_examples.q: From which French verb does entrepreneur derive: enterprendre or entree?

concepts.title: Startup Recognition Eligibility Criteria
concepts.definition: Startup India recognises a venture only while it is young and small: incorporated as a private limited company, partnership or LLP, turnover below one hundred crore rupees in any previous financial year, and no older than ten years from incorporation, working on innovation or improvement rather than being a split-off of an old business.
concepts.key_idea: Subtract the incorporation year from the check year - past ten years or past a hundred crore turnover, the startup tag lapses.
question_patterns: a company was incorporated in 2015 - is it still eligible for startup recognition in 2026 under the ten-year rule
state the turnover ceiling that a recognised startup must not cross in any previous financial year
which legal forms of incorporation qualify an entity for startup recognition
why is an entity formed by splitting up an existing business not considered a startup
under which notification and date are startups defined for the Startup India Action Plan
how many years from incorporation does an entity remain a startup

solution_steps.explain: Startup age is the check year minus the incorporation year.
Subtract the age from the ten-year ceiling to see the recognition time left.

worked_examples.q: Startup India requires turnover below how many crore rupees: one hundred or ten thousand?

concepts.title: Sources of Funds for New Ventures
concepts.definition: A new venture can be fuelled six ways: the entrepreneur's own personal investment that proves commitment, venture capital chasing high-growth technology plays for equity, angel investors - wealthy field leaders - backing early stages with money and mentorship, business incubators or accelerators that host startups for about two years, government grants and subsidies, and bank loans that demand a solid business plan plus personal guarantee.
concepts.key_idea: Seed money follows conviction - personal funds first, angels and incubators early, venture capital and banks once the plan is proven.
question_patterns: list the six sources of financing a new venture with one feature of each
why does an entrepreneur invest personal money first before approaching other investors
differentiate venture capital from angel investment on the stage and nature of funding
how long does a typical incubation phase last and who runs incubation centres
what must complement a good idea before a bank sanctions a startup loan
which funding source takes an equity position in a high-risk technology venture

solution_steps.explain: Personal investment and angels seed the idea; incubators nurse it; venture capital and banks scale it.
Venture capital takes equity; banks take guarantees; grants ask only for outcomes.
Choose the source by stage, amount and the entrepreneur's appetite for dilution or debt.

worked_examples.q: Wealthy field leaders backing early stages with money and mentorship are called what investors: angel or venture?

concepts.title: Biotech versus General Entrepreneur
concepts.definition: Bio-entrepreneurship weds science to commerce, and the union is demanding: long gestation periods, high capital needs, inherent scientific uncertainty layered on business risk, very high academic qualification and a heavy regulatory framework - the points where a biotech entrepreneur parts ways with the general entrepreneur who shares only competitiveness, teamwork and perseverance.
concepts.key_idea: Same grit as any founder, plus a laboratory's timeline, budget, regulators and degrees - that is the biotech premium.
question_patterns: compare a general entrepreneur and a biotech entrepreneur on gestation period and capital requirements
why does a biotech venture carry scientific uncertainty in addition to business uncertainty
why is academic qualification very highly relevant for a biotech entrepreneur
define bio-entrepreneurship as given by A D Meyers
which regulatory load distinguishes biotechnology enterprises from general enterprises
state three reasons why biotech entrepreneurs start their companies

solution_steps.explain: Both need competitive ideas, experienced teams and perseverance through risk.
Gestation, capital, scientific uncertainty, academic depth and regulation run high only in biotech.
A biotech roadmap must budget years of research and regulatory clearance before revenue.

worked_examples.q: Does bio-entrepreneurship carry longer or shorter gestation than general ventures?

concepts.title: Bharat Biotech Case Study
concepts.definition: Dr Krishna Ella's Bharat Biotech, seeded in Hyderabad in 1997 with angel funds, has shipped over four billion vaccine doses to more than a hundred and twenty developing countries, and its seventeenth vaccine - the inactivated whole-virus COVAXIN - went from bench to India's first indigenous COVID-19 shot in a record eight months, winning WHO emergency use listing since December 2020.
concepts.key_idea: Subtract the founding year from the product year to time a company's journey; divide total doses by countries to gauge its reach.
question_patterns: Bharat Biotech was established in 1997 and launched COVAXIN in 2020 - how many years did that journey take
over 4 billion doses reached more than 120 countries - estimate the average doses per country
who founded Bharat Biotech and in which city was the first laboratory set up
in how many months was COVAXIN developed and what type of vaccine is it
which funding source helped establish BBIL and what was its prime objective
which number in Bharat Biotech's portfolio is COVAXIN and when did WHO approve it for emergency use

solution_steps.explain: Journey length is product year minus founding year.
Divide total doses by the number of recipient countries.

worked_examples.q: In which city was Bharat Biotech seeded in 1997: Hyderabad or Delhi?

concepts.title: IPR and Patent Criteria in Biotechnology
concepts.definition: Intellectual property rights guard biotech innovation under the TRIPS framework: Indian patents rest on the Patents Act 1970, whose Section 5 was deleted by the 2005 amendment to admit product patents in biotechnology, chemicals and pharmaceuticals, and a grant demands novelty, an inventive step that is non-obvious, and utility - never landing in Section 3's negative list or offending public order, with discoveries left unpatentable while inventions qualify.
concepts.key_idea: Novel, non-obvious, useful - and an invention, not a discovery - is the four-point test every biotech patent must pass.
question_patterns: state the three central criteria for the grant of a patent on a scientific invention
which amendment of which year allowed product patents in biotechnology in India
differentiate an invention from a discovery under Indian patent law
why was India obliged to amend the Patents Act after joining TRIPS
what role does Section 3 of the Patents Act play in screening biotech inventions
name the committee whose report shaped the Patents Act 1970 and the older law it replaced

solution_steps.explain: The invention must be new against all prior art worldwide.
It must not be obvious to a person skilled in the art.
It must work and stay outside Section 3's negative list and public-order limits.

worked_examples.q: Indian patents rest on which act: the Patents Act 1970 or the Patents Act 1870?

concepts.title: Plant Breeder Rights Protection Years
concepts.definition: Plant breeder's rights hand a new variety's exclusive commercial market for roughly twenty to twenty-five years - provided the variety is novel, distinct, uniform and stable - blocking unauthorised growing or selling of the variety or its reproductive material while sparing research use and the farmer's saved seed.
concepts.key_idea: Average the protection window's ends for a typical term, then subtract elapsed years to see what remains.
question_patterns: plant breeder rights run for 20 to 25 years - compute the midpoint of this protection window
a breeder obtained rights 8 years ago on a 25-year term - how many years of protection remain
which four qualities must a plant variety show to earn breeder's rights
what two exceptions survive plant breeder protection for researchers and farmers
what do plant breeder rights stop others from doing without the owner's permission
differentiate plant breeder rights from farmer's saved seed exemption

solution_steps.explain: Midpoint of the term range is the typical protection length.
Subtract elapsed years from the granted term.

worked_examples.q: Plant breeder's rights run roughly twenty to how many years: twenty-five or five?

concepts.title: Biopiracy Cases and Traditional Knowledge
concepts.definition: Biopiracy is the commercial grab of naturally occurring biochemicals or genetic material riding on indigenous knowledge - the neem pesticide patent W R Grace and the USDA took in the 1990s until the EPO revoked it in 2000, the 1995 University of Mississippi turmeric wound-healing patent the CSIR toppled in 1997, and RiceTec's 1997 Basmati claims partly struck down - with India's Traditional Knowledge Digital Library now standing guard at international patent offices.
concepts.key_idea: Old knowledge cannot be a new invention - documented traditional use, TKDL and geographical indications are the shields.
question_patterns: define biopiracy and name the traditional knowledge domains most often targeted
which companies patented neem oil extraction and in which year did the EPO revoke it
how did CSIR overturn the turmeric wound-healing patent granted in 1995
what was the Basmati rice dispute and which claims of the patent were challenged
what is the Traditional Knowledge Digital Library and against what does it guard
why does biopiracy threaten the livelihood of indigenous communities and farmers
how do geographical indications protect traditional products such as Basmati

solution_steps.explain: A patent claimed over material or use long known to indigenous communities marks biopiracy.
Ancient texts, publications and databases like TKDL destroy the novelty claim.
Geographical indications, community rights and TKDL entries prevent the next grab.

worked_examples.q: Which body toppled the turmeric wound-healing patent in 1997: the CSIR or the USDA?

worked_examples.source_ref: lebt113.txt section 13.2 (startup up to 10 years from incorporation)
worked_examples.question_pattern: A company incorporated in {incorporation_year} applies for startup recognition in {check_year}. Find its startup age and the years of recognition eligibility still left under the ten-year rule.

solution_template.explain: Startup age equals check year minus incorporation year.
Ten years minus the age gives the recognition time left.

worked_examples.source_ref: lebt113.txt Box 2 (BBIL founded 1997, COVAXIN in 2020, 4 billion doses, 120 countries)
worked_examples.question_pattern: Bharat Biotech was founded in {founding_year} and launched COVAXIN in {product_year}; it has supplied {total_doses} vaccine doses across {countries} countries. Find the years from founding to COVAXIN and the average doses per country.

solution_template.explain: The journey length is product year minus founding year.
Total doses divided by countries averages the supply.
